Edit list of Series in the box. Rules:
  • Each Series Prefix on a new line.
  • Allowed special characters are "/" and "-"
  • Optionally, set the number of digits in the series using dot (.) followed by hashes (#). For example, ".####" means that the series will have four digits. Default is five digits.
  • You can also use variables in the series name by putting them between (.) dots
    Supported Variables:
    • .YYYY. - Year in 4 digits
    • .YY. - Year in 2 digits
    • .MM. - Month
    • .DD. - Day of month
    • .WW. - Week of the year
    • .{fieldname}. - fieldname on the document e.g. branch
    • .FY. - Fiscal Year (requires ERPNext to be installed)
    • .ABBR. - Company Abbreviation (requires ERPNext to be installed)

definition.description: One entry on the dock. `link_type` says what kind of thing it opens, and each kind answers the two questions a click asks -- which page comes up and which shell comes up beside it -- in its own way. A `Sidebar` row *is* the shell: it selects that sidebar and opens its landing route. A `Workspace` row opens a page and derives its shell from the module that owns it. A `URL` row leaves the desk and has no shell at all. Every row also carries its own `icon` and `title`, so the rail reads the way its author wrote it -- blank at an upper layer means inherit. What a row points at *is* its identity, and none of it is stored: re-labelling cannot detach a row from itself, and re-pointing is not an edit but a different row. The same rows at all three layers -- the app's own dock, the site's arrangement and one person's -- told apart by the parent `Dock`, never by the row.

fields.description: What kind of thing this entry opens. Spelled the way `Sidebar Item` spells it, so `frappe.ui.sidebar_item.get_route(row)` takes the two page kinds unchanged. `Sidebar` is a value here because a module entry is an entry like any other: it opens the shell, which is the one destination that is not a page.
fields.label: Link Type

fields.description: The record this entry opens, in the doctype `link_type` names. A `Sidebar` target need not exist as a document: most modules have a computed base and no `Sidebar` row at all, so a row of that kind names a shell rather than referencing one, which is why link validation on a `Dock` is a deliberate no-op.

fields.description: Where a web address entry goes. A URL row has no shell and is gated by nothing.

fields.description: What the rail draws this entry with. Required when the row *adds* an entry, because nothing below it holds one; optional when it references an entry a lower layer already has, where blank means inherit and filled is an override.

fields.description: How this entry reads on the rail. Required when the row adds and optional when it references, exactly as `icon` is -- and outside the row's identity, so re-labelling can never detach a row from itself.

fields.description: This row *is* the entry, rather than an opinion about one a lower layer holds. Stored rather than inferred from the row carrying a body: under partial opinions a reference may carry an icon and no title, so body-presence stops telling the two apart -- and a reference to a row the app has since deleted would resurrect as a label-less button.

fields.label: Print Format Help
fields.options:
Print Format Help

Introduction

Print Formats are rendered on the server side using the Jinja Templating Language. All forms have access to the doc object which contains information about the document that is being formatted. You can also access common utilities via the frappe module.

For styling, the Boostrap CSS framework is provided and you can enjoy the full range of classes.

References

  1. Jinja Templating Language
  2. Bootstrap CSS Framework

Example

<h3>{{ doc.select_print_heading or "Invoice" }}</h3>
<div class="row">
	<div class="col-md-3 text-right">Customer Name</div>
	<div class="col-md-9">{{ doc.customer_name }}</div>
</div>
<div class="row">
	<div class="col-md-3 text-right">Date</div>
	<div class="col-md-9">{{ doc.get_formatted("invoice_date") }}</div>
</div>
<table class="table table-bordered">
	<tbody>
		<tr>
			<th>Sr</th>
			<th>Item Name</th>
			<th>Description</th>
			<th class="text-right">Qty</th>
			<th class="text-right">Rate</th>
			<th class="text-right">Amount</th>
		</tr>
		{%- for row in doc.items -%}
		<tr>
			<td style="width: 3%;">{{ row.idx }}</td>
			<td style="width: 20%;">
				{{ row.item_name }}
				{% if row.item_code != row.item_name -%}
				<br>Item Code: {{ row.item_code}}
				{%- endif %}
			</td>
			<td style="width: 37%;">
				<div style="border: 0px;">{{ row.description }}</div></td>
			<td style="width: 10%; text-align: right;">{{ row.qty }} {{ row.uom or row.stock_uom }}</td>
			<td style="width: 15%; text-align: right;">{{
				row.get_formatted("rate", doc) }}</td>
			<td style="width: 15%; text-align: right;">{{
				row.get_formatted("amount", doc) }}</td>
		</tr>
		{%- endfor -%}
	</tbody>
</table>

Common Functions

doc.get_formatted("[fieldname]", [parent_doc]) Get document value formatted as Date, Currency, etc. Pass parent doc for currency type fields.
frappe.db.get_value("[doctype]", "[name]", "fieldname") Get value from another document.
